note: An invented epic: a 16-item ask for an invented habit-tracker CLI and 12 tickets for it. Items 13-16 have no ticket; 10-12 do. The tickets are deliberately out of ask order (ticket 1 covers item 2, ticket 4 item 12, tickets 5-12 items 4-11), so only matching by content finds them. Used by the ask-items-uncovered plan check test.
ask:
Tidepool epic 2: reporting and polish for a terminal habit tracker (repo ~/work/tidepool after epic 1; gate `npm run verify`; Node built-ins only). Evidence from a hands-on trial and a spec audit, quoted per item. One ticket per item, numbered acceptance, tests that fail without the change, "(operator)" for live checks; order tickets sharing a file serially.

1. Streak sparklines. `tide stats` prints a table of counts only. Add a unicode sparkline of the last 30 days beside each habit, one block character per day, scaled to that habit's own daily target; an empty day is a blank, never a zero-height bar. Golden output for the three sample habits.
2. CSV export. `tide export --csv` does not exist. Write one row per check-in with the columns habit, date, note, and quote any field that holds a comma or a newline; the header row is always printed, even with no check-ins. Fixture tests.
3. Quiet hours for reminders. The reminders config fires nudges at any hour. Add quietStart and quietEnd keys; a nudge that falls inside the window is deferred to quietEnd, including a window that crosses midnight. Reject a config where the two keys are equal, with the key names in the message.
4. Duplicate habit names. `tide add Run` succeeds when `run` already exists, and the two then collide in stats. Compare names case-insensitively, refuse the second with `a habit named run already exists`, and print the existing habit's start date.
5. Backdated check-ins. `tide done run --on 2026-01-03` is rejected as an unknown option. Accept an ISO date no later than today and no earlier than the habit's start; say which bound failed. A backdated check-in must not double count a day that already has one.
6. Archive command. A retired habit can only be deleted, which loses its history. Add `tide archive <habit>` that hides it from the daily list and from stats but keeps every check-in, and `tide archive --list` that shows what is hidden.
7. Day rollover after a clock change. The day boundary is computed from a fixed 24-hour offset, so the day after a daylight-saving change is counted twice or skipped. Use local midnight from the calendar, and add fixtures for the spring and the autumn change.
8. Colour output. `tide stats` always prints ANSI colour, even into a pipe. Honour NO_COLOR and a non-terminal stdout, and add a `--color=always|never|auto` option that overrides both.
9. Shell completion. Add `tide completion bash` and `tide completion zsh`, printing a script that completes subcommands and, for done and archive, the names of active habits read from the data file.
10. Weekly targets. A habit can only mean once a day. Accept `--every 3/week` on add, count a week as Monday to Sunday, and show `2 of 3 this week` in the daily list. A target above 7 per week is refused.
11. Import from CSV. `tide import habits.csv` should load rows in the shape the export writes. Skip a row whose habit and date already exist, report how many rows were added and how many were skipped, and refuse the whole file when the header is wrong.
12. Unknown habit errors. `tide done rnu` prints a stack trace. Print `no habit named rnu - did you mean run?` using the closest active name within an edit distance of two, list the active names when none is close, and exit 2.
13. A small web dashboard. `tide serve` starts a local page on port 4300 that charts the streaks, refreshes every minute, and binds to loopback only.
14. Cloud backup. Add an upload of the data file to a configured bucket after every check-in, with retry and a status line in `tide stats`; the credentials come from the environment.
15. Native installer. Ship a signed package for Windows with a start-menu entry, and an uninstaller that leaves the data directory alone.
16. Reference page. Generate a manual page from the command table, install it with the package, and fail the build when a command lacks a description.

tickets.title: CSV export of check-ins
tickets.acceptance: 1. `tide export --csv` writes one row per check-in with the columns habit, date, note. 2. A field holding a comma, a quote or a newline is quoted and round-trips through a plain parser. 3. The header row is printed even when there are no check-ins. 4. The tests fail without the change. 5. npm run verify passes.

tickets.title: Streak sparklines in tide stats
tickets.acceptance: 1. The hand-written golden output for the three sample habits matches exactly (habit, sparkline, count), and the diff shows the goldens were not dumped from the new code. 2. One block character per day for the last 30 days, scaled to each habit's own daily target. 3. An empty day is a blank, never a zero-height bar. 4. The other columns of `tide stats` are unchanged and their existing tests pass. 5. The new tests fail without the change. 6. npm run verify passes. 7. (operator) In a terminal, the sparklines line up under the header for a habit with a long name.

tickets.title: Quiet hours for reminders: quietStart and quietEnd
tickets.acceptance:
1. A nudge that falls inside the quiet window is deferred to quietEnd, and one outside it fires on time. 2. A window that crosses midnight (22:00 to 07:00) defers a 23:30 nudge and a 02:00 nudge. 3. A config where quietStart equals quietEnd is rejected, and the message names both keys. 4. The tests fail without the change. 5. npm run verify passes.
6. OPERATOR ADDITION (senior review): the window logic lives in one function that the scheduler and the config check both call, with a test for each caller.
7. OPERATOR ADDITION (senior review): (operator) with a real reminder set for two minutes inside the window, no nudge appears until quietEnd.

tickets.title: Unknown habit: a plain message with a suggestion
tickets.acceptance: 1. `tide done rnu` prints `no habit named rnu - did you mean run?` and exits 2, with no stack trace. 2. The suggestion is the closest active name within an edit distance of two. 3. When no name is close, the message lists the active names. 4. The same message is used by done, archive and export. 5. Each item has a CLI test that fails without the change. 6. npm run verify passes.

tickets.title: Refuse duplicate habit names, case-insensitively
tickets.acceptance:
1. `tide add Run` after `run` exists exits 2 and prints `a habit named run already exists`. 2. The message includes the start date of the existing habit. 3. `tide add Runner` is still accepted. 4. The data file is not touched by a refused add. 5. The tests fail without the change. 6. npm run verify passes.
7. OPERATOR ADDITION (senior review): the comparison is a rule in the shared name normaliser (not an ad-hoc lowercase); add, archive and done all use it, with a test for each command.

tickets.title: Backdated check-ins with --on
tickets.acceptance:
1. `tide done run --on 2026-01-03` records the check-in on that date. 2. A date in the future is refused and the message says it is later than today. 3. A date before the habit's start is refused and the message says it is earlier than the start. 4. A backdated check-in on a day that already has one does not double count. 5. The tests fail without the change. 6. npm run verify passes.
7. OPERATOR ADDITION (senior review): the date check is a rule in the shared date parser created by the day-rollover ticket (not an ad-hoc comparison); done and export both use it, with a test for each command.

tickets.title: Archive habits without losing history
tickets.acceptance:
1. `tide archive run` hides the habit from the daily list and from stats. 2. Every check-in of an archived habit is still in the data file and in the CSV export. 3. `tide archive --list` shows exactly the hidden habits. 4. Archiving an unknown habit exits 2 with the standard unknown-habit message. 5. The tests fail without the change. 6. npm run verify passes.
7. OPERATOR ADDITION (senior review): the hidden flag is read through one accessor, so a later command cannot forget it; stats, the daily list and completion all use it, with a test for each.

tickets.title: Day boundary from local midnight, not a 24-hour offset
tickets.acceptance:
1. The spring fixture counts the day after the clock change once, not twice. 2. The autumn fixture counts the repeated hour as one day, not two. 3. A check-in at 23:59 and one at 00:01 fall on different days in both fixtures. 4. The data file format is unchanged. 5. The tests fail without the change. 6. npm run verify passes.
7. OPERATOR ADDITION (senior review): implemented as the shared date parser that other commands reuse (not a per-command fix); done, stats and export all call it, with a test for each command.

tickets.title: Honour NO_COLOR and pipes; add --color
tickets.acceptance: 1. With stdout piped, `tide stats` prints no escape sequences. 2. With NO_COLOR set, a terminal run prints none either. 3. `--color=always` forces colour in a pipe and `--color=never` removes it on a terminal, and both win over NO_COLOR. 4. An invalid `--color` value exits 2 and lists the three accepted values. 5. The tests fail without the change. 6. npm run verify passes.

tickets.title: Shell completion scripts for bash and zsh
tickets.acceptance:
1. `tide completion bash` and `tide completion zsh` each print a script that completes every subcommand. 2. For done and archive the script completes the names of active habits read from the data file, and never an archived one. 3. An unknown shell name exits 2 and lists the two supported shells. 4. The tests run each script in a subshell and fail without the change. 5. npm run verify passes.
6. OPERATOR ADDITION (senior review): the subcommand list is generated from the command table, not typed a second time, with a test that adds a command and sees it completed.

tickets.title: Weekly targets: --every N/week
tickets.acceptance: 1. `tide add swim --every 3/week` stores the target, and the daily list shows `2 of 3 this week` after two check-ins. 2. A week runs Monday to Sunday, and a Sunday check-in does not count toward the next week. 3. A target above 7 per week is refused with exit 2. 4. A habit without --every behaves exactly as before. 5. The tests fail without the change. 6. npm run verify passes.

tickets.title: Import check-ins from CSV
tickets.acceptance: 1. `tide import habits.csv` loads rows in the shape the export writes, and an export followed by an import into an empty data file reproduces the original. 2. A row whose habit and date already exist is skipped. 3. The summary says how many rows were added and how many were skipped. 4. A file with a wrong header is refused as a whole and the data file is untouched. 5. The tests fail without the change. 6. npm run verify passes.
